name: Four Knights Game
summary: The Four Knights Game (1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Nc3 Nf6) develops all four knights in a sound, classical Open Game.
intro: The Four Knights Game arises after 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Nc3 Nf6, with both sides calmly developing every knight before committing the bishops. It is among the most natural and principled of the Open Games, offering everything from the quiet, symmetrical Spanish lines to the fireworks of the Belgrade and Halloween gambits.
line: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Nc3 Nf6

sections.heading: Strategic ideas
paragraphs: The Four Knights Game is defined by rapid, symmetrical piece development: after 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Nc3 Nf6 all four knights are in play and both armies fight for the central squares d4, d5, e4 and e5. Because the structure is balanced, the opening has a deserved reputation for soundness, and it is a natural choice for players who value clear development and healthy pawns over early complications.

White's central aim is often to prepare d4, either directly or after Bb5, using the extra tempo of the first move to press for a small but lasting initiative. Black, in turn, looks for a moment to break the symmetry favourably — most famously with ...Nd4 and ...Bxc3 ideas — so that the position does not simply peter out into a lifeless draw. Whoever handles the transition from symmetry to imbalance more accurately usually seizes the initiative.

sections.heading: Main variations
paragraphs: The classical main line is the Spanish Four Knights, 4.Bb5, borrowing ideas from the Ruy López and often leading to symmetrical, manoeuvring positions after 4...Bb4. Black's most combative reply is the Rubinstein Variation, 4...Nd4, immediately challenging the b5-bishop and inviting sharp play. The quieter Glek System, 4.g3, fianchettoing the bishop, is a modern, positional way to fight for an edge.

Sharper tries abound. The Scotch Four Knights, 4.d4, opens the centre at once, while the Belgrade Gambit, 4.d4 exd4 5.Nd5, sacrifices a pawn for rapid development and attacking chances. Most extreme of all is the Halloween Gambit, 4.Nxe5, a speculative knight sacrifice that throws Black's pieces backward and aims for a crushing pawn storm in the centre — objectively dubious but dangerous over the board.

sections.heading: History and background
paragraphs: The Four Knights Game was one of the most popular openings of the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries, appearing frequently in the games of attacking masters such as Emanuel Lasker and Joseph Henry Blackburne. Its reputation for solidity later saw it recede at the very top level, but modern grandmasters — Igor Glek among them — have periodically revived it as a low-theory, strategically rich weapon that still poses practical problems.
